section_7_verdict.conclusion: H-GRAPH-01 REFUTED: graph_proximity_weight=0.2 produces no improvement in hit@10 on 855 graph-sensitive probe pairs (Cliff's δ=0.000, CI=[0,0], p=0.500). NULL RESULT IS PUBLISHABLE per §7 criterion. Root cause (architectural): probe targets (cosine 0.225-0.336 from seeds) fall outside recall_hybrid's candidate pool (top-100). Graph proximity is a re-ranking signal for already-retrieved candidates — it cannot inject graph-walked nodes into results. For graph benefit to be measurable, probe design must select targets within top-40-100 candidates but outside top-10 (i.e., cosine 0.7-0.9 range, not <0.7).

architectural_finding.title: recall_hybrid graph proximity is re-rank-only, not candidate injection
architectural_finding.detail: recall_hybrid computes graph proximity for nodes in all_candidates (union of vec_candidates and bm25_candidates). Nodes reachable via graph_walk but NOT in all_candidates receive no proximity score and cannot appear in results. For the probe design (cosine<0.7), probe targets are outside top-100 by cosine similarity and typically absent from bm25_candidates. Therefore graph_walk cannot surface them regardless of δ. To measure true graph recall benefit: either (A) revise probe design to cosine 0.7-0.9 range (target in candidate pool but outside top-10), OR (B) revise recall_hybrid to include depth-1 graph-walked nodes as third candidate source alongside vec/bm25.
